You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Sears Holdings / acquired going-concern business realized record, ~2022-2024 horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired going-concern business passed
> to a privately held buyer and the seller ceased periodic reporting, there is no
> post-closing public annual report; the realized record is traced through the reporting-
> status filings and reputable press. This sub-dossier contains no information about how
> the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- The buyer of the going concern, Transform Holdco LLC, is a privately held affiliate of
  ESL Investments and files no periodic reports with the SEC; the acquired retail business
  therefore has no public audited annual report within the outcome window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-016016, 8-K Item 1.01]
- Sears Holdings Corporation's last Annual Report on Form 10-K on EDGAR is for fiscal 2017,
  filed March 23, 2018; no Form 10-K covering fiscal 2018 (year ended early February 2019)
  or any later fiscal year was filed. [SRC: SEC accession 0001310067-18-000006, Form 10-K]
- On April 18, 2019 Sears Holdings filed a Form 15 (15-15D) certifying termination of
  registration / suspension of its duty to file reports for the covered securities classes,
  stating approximately 67 holders of record as of the notice date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-111058, Form 15-15D]
- Consequently, no audited public financial statements exist for the ~2022-2024 outcome
  window, and the realized-record facts below rely on reputable press rather than primary
  SEC filings. [SRC: SEC accession 0001310067-18-000006, Form 10-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-111058, Form 15-15D]

## Realized record under private ownership (press-sourced)
- Under private ownership (styled "Transformco"), the acquired retail footprint continued
  to contract: a reputable trade-press account dated January 24, 2022 reported that
  research firm Coresight counted 46 announced Sears closures and 29 announced Kmart
  closures during 2021, with Transformco owning both banners. [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/sears-gets-smaller-with-florida-store-closure/617572]
- The same account identifies Eddie Lampert as the last CEO of Sears Holdings and majority
  owner of the company in the years leading up to its 2018 bankruptcy filing. [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/sears-gets-smaller-with-florida-store-closure/617572]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Aggregated tallies of "remaining" full-line Sears stores reported by secondary press for
  2024-2025 are not traceable to any audited primary financial statement and are not relied
  on here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the going-concern business passed to a private affiliate (Transform Holdco /
  Transformco) and Sears Holdings ceased filing periodic reports (last Form 10-K fiscal
  2017; Form 15 filed April 2019), there is no public audited outcome record for the
  ~2022-2024 window; the case is coded **UNCERTAIN** on the outcome. The only traceable
  realized signal is reputable press indicating continued contraction of the acquired
  store base under private ownership. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-19-111058, Form 15-15D] [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/sears-gets-smaller-with-florida-store-closure/617572]

[SLICE END]
